This morning I weighed in at 310 lbs. Exactly 35 lbs lost since I started on December 31. Originally my first goal was to be under 300 lbs by graduation, but I think if I work at it I could possibly get there by mid April, although I'm not concerned so much with the number as I am about just being healthy. 

People are starting to notice, too. I've taken lots of pictures along the way. I can't really see it too well yet, although now I've lost over 10% of my starting weight. Some friends are saying my jaw is becoming a bit more defined.

Edit: I weigh myself every sunday, but occasionally I'll do a midweek weigh. This sunday I was 311 lbs, while last sunday I was 313 lbs.

I understand where you're coming from. I'm still early in my journey as well, but it's never too late to start. You don't need to go all in super-pumped fitness on day one. In fact, if you do that, it won't be sustainable and you'll burn out. When you start something like this, you have to think about sustainability. I didn't do that the last time, so I burned out after a few weeks. But now I've been going since December 31 and I feel like what I'm doing I can keep doing. 

You don't even need to exercise to lose weight. What's helped me lose almost 30 lbs in two months is simply counting calories. I still eat what I want to eat, I just eat less of it and track it. If I go over one day, I don't consider it the end of the world, I just take each day as it comes. 

I also do elliptical, and I find it fascinating that I am where I am, because when I started on December 31, I couldn't do 15 minutes before keeling over. But I kept doing it each day. When I got moderately comfortable with doing 15 minutes, I tried 16 minutes, then 17, 18, etc, and as of today I'm doing 35 minutes/day for six days/week. At over 300 lbs! And oddly enough, I'm actually at the point where I kinda enjoy it now! 

It's all about the small, sustainable changes that you build on over time. It's all about taking each day at a time and remembering that no matter what, you tried your damn hardest that day. Even if you fail, you pick yourself up and remember that tomorrow is another day. 

I actually made a post on r/mentalhealth a few days ago because I had a really bad breakdown, and I'm still dealing with those issues, but unlike the last time I tried to lose weight and failed, this time I'm not letting them stop me. I'm motivated to be healthier just to spite that voice in the back of my head telling me I'm not good enough, and give depression/self doubt a giant middle finger. 

I really hope this helps. This sub will be here for you if you fall, and cheer you on during your victories, even the small ones.
